acceptance: Red-first: ResumeReady with a future +0800 value is false and with a past one is true.
The seed of the test comes from the real writer (the bench reset path), not a hand-written RFC3339 string.
100% coverage on each changed function; zero code comments; checkpoint-resume.md names the format.
fix: Write the reset time in one format, or parse both layouts in one helper that the writer and ResumeReady share. Treat an unparsable non-empty value as a logged warning, not silently as ready.
routed_reason: built by a claude-cloud bridge seat in the operator credit window on 2026-11-04
source: console 2026-11-04: cycle 2147's checkpoint holds quotaResetAt 2026-11-04T08:53:30+0800 (source bench). ResumeReady (PR #1280) parses time.RFC3339, which rejects an offset with no colon, and it reads a parse error as ready. The test fixtures used RFC3339, so no test saw it.
summary: A pause that waits for a known reset is put first in the pool backlog before its quota returns, which is what ResumeReady exists to prevent. The order hint is silently off for each bench-sourced reset time. Admission is not affected.
title: checkpoint.ResumeReady treats a future reset as ready because the checkpoint writes +0800, not RFC3339
